title: Threshold and the sodium channel
objective: Explain how voltage-gated sodium channels create threshold and why Nav1.7 and Nav1.8 matter for pain.

steps.title: The positive-feedback switch
steps.body:
**[[voltage-gated sodium channel|Voltage-gated Na⁺ channels]]** (Nav) open when the membrane depolarizes. Their opening lets Na⁺ in, which depolarizes the membrane further and opens more of them.

**[[threshold|Threshold]]** is the voltage where this loop becomes self-sustaining and an action potential takes off.

visual.alt: A voltage-versus-time trace of one action potential: it rests near −70 mV, a stimulus reaches the −55 mV threshold, sodium flows in and the voltage spikes to about +30 mV, then potassium flows out and it falls back past rest before recovering.
visual.caption: Na⁺ in drives the upstroke; K⁺ out brings it back down.

steps.title: Inactivation and the refractory period
steps.body:
Within about a millisecond Nav channels **inactivate**: they close and can't reopen until the membrane repolarizes. Meanwhile, voltage-gated K⁺ channels repolarize the cell.

Inactivation causes the **[[refractory period]]**. It caps maximum firing rate and makes spikes travel one way.

steps.title: Nav1.7 and Nav1.8: the pain channels
steps.body:
DRG neurons express several Nav subtypes:

- **[[Nav1.7]]** amplifies small depolarizations toward threshold. People with loss-of-function mutations in its gene (*SCN9A*) are born unable to feel pain; gain-of-function mutations cause severe pain disorders.
- **[[Nav1.8]]** is enriched in nociceptors and is resistant to the toxin TTX. Its Cre line (`Scn10a-Cre`, often called Nav1.8-Cre) is a widely used way to target many nociceptors.

flag.note: Nav1.8-Cre labels a broad population that includes more than nociceptors; check specificity for your tissue.

pairs: Sets pain sensitivity; loss means no pain
steps.explanation: These are the core facts behind both pain biology and some of the most common sensory-neuron Cre lines.

steps.setup: Inflammation shifts nociceptor Nav channels so they open at slightly more negative voltages.
steps.prompt: What happens to the neuron's excitability?
options: Increases: threshold is effectively lower, so weaker stimuli trigger spikes
The neuron can no longer fire
steps.reveal: A lower effective threshold means smaller receptor potentials are enough to fire. That is one mechanism of peripheral sensitization (A9), and why inflamed tissue hurts to the touch.
